steps.text: Combine rice and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to low, cover with lid, and allow to steam until tender, about 20 minutes.

While rice is cooking, grind peanuts in a blender and set aside. Heat the margarine in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in the onion; cook and stir until the onion has softened and turned golden brown about 10 minutes. Stir in ginger, carrots, and salt to taste. Reduce heat to low and cover to steam 5 minutes. Stir in cayenne pepper and peanuts. When rice is done, add it to skillet and stir gently to combine with other ingredients. Garnish with chopped cilantro.

review.reviewBody: This was an excellent alternative to plain rice. Here were the changes I made: I steamed my rice, tried almonds instead of peanuts first and then tried peanuts and my husband and I both prefered ground almonds instead. Added 1/4 tsp of cayenne pepper because we love it spicy! Used 3/4 tsp of ground ginger. Used a good amount of salt and left out the cilantro, but I'm sure this would be an excellent garnish but didn't have it on hand. Made this with cajun snapper. Will cook this many more times. Thanks Sowmya :)

We all liked this. Notes on a few other reviews; it's best to use a microplane on the ginger instead of hand mincing. It will be much finer and the flavor will incorporate better into the dish. I made this without the peanuts since I'm eating peanut-free. I think I'll try almonds next time because the crunch could add a nice touch. I also only did a dash of cayenne. My family doesn't mind spicy, so I definitely went too light as we couldn't even tell the cayenne was in the dish. I doubled the recipe and my family of 5 (3 boys, 2 of which are teenagers) finished most of it. :) Other note, I used jasmine rice because it's all I had on hand. I will try next time with basmati and see which we like best! I did the rice in the rice cooker and it made it quick. While it was cooking I did the pan of the other ingredients and just combined by using tongs to mix well. We will definitely have this again and it will probably be added to our regular rotation.

The hardest part about this is grating the carrots. Otherwise, very simple and tasty dish. I doubled the carrots using the medium grate on my grater. I simply eyeballed the ginger but probably added extra (how did it take me this long to learn about freezing ginger and grating as needed? Wow, is that easy). I also did a heaping 1/4 cup of peanuts, and didn't quite use all the cooked rice as I wanted a more vegetable dish than rice. It is so good! I noticed some added chicken broth in, but I don't think that would add to it - at least in my opinion. I followed the comments/directions to cover the pan after adding the carrots and ginger to let them steam to softness. I actually turned the heat off entirely during that time and just let it sit for the full five minutes. The carrots were soft and there was some moisture still remaining when I removed the lid. I typically like to doctor things up, but this, for me, is one of a few that I think I like the way it is (but with more carrots!). Quite satisfying.

To try my new instant pressure cooker pot, I tried this using what vegetables I had. On sauté setting I cooked chopped green onion and celery in a little oil, then added sliced almonds, and later 2 cups jasmine rice. After sautéing slightly, I added 2 1/2 cups of chicken broth (I had just boiled chicken) in to the pot, 1 t of chicken bouillon powder, stirred everything together and set the pot to rice setting. This cooked for 15 min after reaching the steam setting. The rice was light and not gummed together like it sometimes does for me when cooked on the stove top. We enjoyed the dish and I want to try it next time with the carrot and ginger. Thank you for such a fun and versatile recipe that lends itself well to so many diff veggies. Bet it would also be good with either green beans or peas and carrots or mushrooms.

I did not add the nuts. I used virgin coconut oil to fry a batch of green onions, the grated carrots with a subtle 1/3 tsp of powdered ginger and the same of dried cilantro my leftover white rice from last night's Chinese take-out. I added so much rice that I had to up the amount of coconut oil, to get it to be not as dry. The coconut flavor and aroma was great in this dish! Everyone raved.

This recipe is good. I will make it again. However, I made it without the peanuts since the hubby does not like them. With that said the actual change I made was in the procedure. I cooked the veggies first starting with the onions, then carrots, and lastly the ginger. Then, I added the rice and broth and let it cook as directed.... My rice came out naturally colored by the carrots and the latter were soft. The flavor was so mild that it blended well with Poulet á la moutarde from this site. Oh and I added the cilantro right before putting on the table. It gave a contrast between all flavors but without being overpowering. Will make it again!!!

This was a truly great recipe!! Easy to make, delicious and so colorful. Will definitely be making many times over. For the rice portion I chose to use Chef John's oven method since I do not seem to make great rice in a pot. I just halved his recipe and made in an 8x8 pan and used chicken broth instead of the noted water in this recipe. I used almonds instead of peanuts but both are great I'm sure. The ginger is subtle but adds such a nice touch. This is definitely a 5 star recipe.

I cooked this recipe twice already. The first time, I cooked it exactly as written and it was good. But the second time I made it, cooked my regular white rice in chicken broth, I added garlic, upped the shredded carrots to a heaping 1 cup, was generous with the grated ginger (used my zester) substituted butter instead of margarine and lightly crumbled the peanuts. Added more chicken broth as necessary at the end when combing rice with veggies. I think this is a great recipe which is easy and versatile. It's on my keeper list.

I'm sure after a few more tries with further tweaking this will be a keeper. Unfortunately my first attempt was a disappointment. I sauteed the onion with some chicken broth as well as a glop of ginger-garlic paste, so I didn't add any ginger with the carrots. Probably next time I will try it in the correct order. I used leftover quinoa and brown rice, along with a mixture of dry roasted (salted) peanuts and raw cashews. I added the cayenne to the nuts beforehand and I liked the spice and texture. Looking forward to tasting it after a night in the fridge to better meld the flavours!

I paired this with Baked Teriyaki Chicken (also on here) and it was delicious! Red onion and dried cilantro was all I had, but it worked great! Also, I sautéed everything in the pan and added it to the rice pot instead of adding rice to sauté pan (just an easier clean up and it mixes better when fluffing rice). I would like to try this with Jasmine rice for the extra flowery flavor JasRice will bring to the dish.

I can't leave a recipe alone, so this is what I did to enhance the original recipe. Used olive oil & butter instead of margarine; added chopped kale with the onions; 2 cloves of minced garlic and 1/2 chopped tomato along with ginger; cashews & almonds instead of peanuts; and drizzled sesame oil over the entire dish when it was all put together. The above ingredients were for two servings. It was very yummy.

I had leftover cold basmati rice. I sautéed the carrot, onion, ginger, salt and cayenne pepper together, added some sesame oil and then added the crushed peanuts and rice. I let it cook about ten minutes partially covered. It is excellent. It’s almost like a Thai fried rice but with less sodium. That’s just what I was looking to achieve.
I added garlic and doubled the recipe. Loved it and I will be making this again!

I have enjoyed this recipe many times, and liked it a lot. I often use it in a chicken burrito with black bean refried beans, shredded chicken, shredded Mexican blend cheese, and of course, I had some hot sauce and sour cream. Yum!
I used wild rice Otherwise did the recipe as is. I did put a little Italian dressing over the top of it.😂
I also substituted sliced almonds for the peanuts. It was a very tasty side. The following day I mixed in a can of black beans with the leftovers, warmed it up and had a great supper dish.

Omg I loved this rice!!!! Delish, I added a bit of left over yellow bell pepper that i had and it was so pretty and flavorful!!! You have to try this!! I always use this recipe when I make the Chicken Tikka Masala recipe on here. Perfect together!!

I followed the recipe exactly. It is delicious! For the cayenne I added only a small dash. Added just a hint of heat. My husband loved it. Recipe easily serves four. Served with seasoned sautéed chicken tenderloins and steamed kale with garlic and white wine. Great combo. I will be making this again.

This recipe is great and can be modified to your taste. I made a similar rice dish many years ago. For extra taste I added more ginger, crushed garlic and cayenne pepper. Just before serving garnished with minced fresh cilantro from my garden and roasted slivered almond and did not use peanuts. It turned out AWESOME and always a crowd pleaser!

My husband and I LOVED it. Everything was so fragrant and delicious. I had some brown basmati rice which tasted great in this dish. My only criticism is the name of the dish. I think it should be called "Thai Fried Rice."
